name: undervolt-cool
description: Low-power / cool-running profile. A USB flash controller does NOT expose a VID voltage offset like a CPU — this profile is the honest translation: lower NAND clock grade, aggressive link power management, modest OP, cool thermal setpoint. Trades peak throughput for lower average power and junction temperature.

capacity_impact.method: usable ≈ advertised × (1 − OP/100) × (1 − pSLC/100). Small pSLC + modest OP keeps most of the capacity.

host_recommendations.partition_scheme: whatever you want — this profile makes no partition demands
notes: Run cooler = last longer. If this drive lives in a laptop case or inside a vehicle, this profile buys you thermal margin.

LPM (Link Power Management) must also be enabled on the host for the full idle-power gain. Linux: `/sys/bus/usb/devices/.../power/control = auto`. macOS: enabled by default. Windows: enable via power plan.
Expect ~20-30% lower peak throughput than factory. Random IO latency may be slightly worse too (NAND clocked lower).
Thermal setpoint 55°C is aggressive — most drives run above this when active. Expect visible throttling under load. That's the point.
